chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yun, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about one who knows nothing, is there any responsibility upon him? He (peace be upon him) replied, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abd Allah (AS), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.لَمْ يَعْرِفْ شَيْئًا: He knows nothing (referring to religious rulings)
key_terms.هَلْ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: Is there any responsibility/burden upon him

ai.seo_question: Does ignorance of religious duties exempt a person from responsibility in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that total ignorance of religious duties exempts an individual from accountability, establishing a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding the conditions of *taklif*. This ruling underscores the divine mercy in legal responsibility, ensuring that obligation is contingent upon the capacity to know, thereby distinguishing between the ignorant layperson and the scholar. It serves as a critical counterpoint to the general rule that knowledge is required for duty, highlighting that absence of knowledge itself removes the burden.
